quips.Cushat: An old Scots name for the wood pigeon.

krillion.quip: The orange-red of a wild poppy — it's simply the French word for poppy.

quips.Puce: French for "flea" — literally the colour of a flea.
quips.Eigengrau: German for "intrinsic grey" — what your eyes see in total darkness.
quips.Gamboge: A mustard-yellow tree resin, named after Cambodia.
quips.Glaucous: The dusty blue-grey bloom you can rub off a plum.

krillion.quip: Makes arrows — from Old French "flèche", meaning arrow.

quips.Cordwainer: A maker of new shoes — cobblers were only allowed to mend them.
quips.Knocker-upper: Before alarm clocks, they tapped on windows with long poles to wake workers.
quips.Tosher: Victorian scavengers who searched London's sewers for lost coins.
quips.Luthier: A maker of stringed instruments — from the French for lute.
quips.Fuller: Pounded wool cloth to thicken it, often by trampling it underfoot.

quips.Tuffet: A low seat or footstool — Little Miss Muffet's famous perch.

krillion.quip: From Persian "kamarband" — literally a loin-band.

quips.Balaclava: Named after the Crimean War battle where British troops wore knitted versions.
quips.Farthingale: A hooped underskirt that made Tudor dresses spread like bells.
quips.Spencer: A cropped jacket named after the 2nd Earl Spencer in the 1790s.

chapters.text: Name a collective noun for a group of animals

krillion.quip: Like many of these, it was popularised by the 15th-century Book of Saint Albans.

quips.Crash (of rhinos): Rhinos can charge at around 30 mph, so a crash feels earned.
quips.Flamboyance (of flamingos): A modern coinage, but too perfect not to catch on.
quips.Bloat (of hippos): Hippos spend most of the day wallowing in water — bloat suits them.

krillion.quip: A Victorian spinning disc that merges two pictures — like a bird into its cage.

quips.Teddy bear: Named after US President Theodore 'Teddy' Roosevelt, who spared a bear on a 1902 hunt.
quips.Slinky: Invented by an engineer who watched a torsion spring tumble off a shelf.
quips.Silly Putty: A failed attempt at synthetic rubber that turned into a bestselling toy.

krillion.quip: A tiny drawstring handbag of Regency ladies — mocked at the time as a 'ridicule'.

quips.Sporran: The pouch worn with a kilt — because kilts have no pockets.
quips.Gladstone bag: Named after the Victorian prime minister William Gladstone.
quips.Bum bag: Americans call it a fanny pack, a phrase that makes Brits blush.
quips.Carpetbag: Made from old carpet — and the origin of 'carpetbagger' in post-Civil War America.

quips.Fez: Named after the Moroccan city of Fez, once the main source of its crimson dye.
quips.Mortarboard: Named for its likeness to a bricklayer's board for holding mortar.

Was it a car or a cat I saw

Rats live on no evil star
Go hang a salami, I'm a lasagna hog
Mr. Owl ate my metal worm
Was it a cat I saw

Ma is a nun, as I am
deepcut: Sit on a potato pan, Otis

Pull up if I pull up

Was it Eliot's toilet I saw

Was it a car or a cat I saw: Was it a car or a cat I saw?

chapters.text: Name a sport that has featured at the Olympics

quips.Monkey pose: Named for Hanuman, the monkey god who leapt from India to Lanka in one bound.

krillion.quip: A blind cave salamander that can go up to a decade without eating.

quips.Glass frog: Its belly skin is see-through, so you can watch its heart beating.
quips.Darwin's frog: Dads raise tadpoles in their vocal sacs, then cough up tiny froglets.
quips.Hairy frog: Breaks its own toe bones to make claws when threatened.

krillion.quip: Discovered in 2005, it grows bacteria on its hairy arms near deep-sea vents.

quips.Coconut crab: The largest land invertebrate, strong enough to crack open coconuts.
quips.Mantis shrimp: Punches so fast it makes bubbles that collapse with a tiny flash of light.
quips.Tongue-eating louse: Replaces a fish's tongue and then lives on in its mouth.
quips.Japanese spider crab: Its legs can span nearly 4 metres from claw to claw.

krillion.quip: The first element ever made artificially; its name is Greek for 'artificial'.

quips.Hafnium: Named after Copenhagen, whose old Latin name is Hafnia.
quips.Gallium: Melts in your hand: it turns liquid at about 30 °C.
quips.Oganesson: The heaviest element known, and only a handful of atoms have ever existed.

chapters.text: Name a bone in the human body

krillion.quip: A tiny wrist bone whose name literally means 'pea-shaped'.

quips.Hyoid: The only bone in your body not attached to any other bone.
quips.Stapes: The smallest bone in the body, shaped like a stirrup in your ear.
quips.Fabella: A little sesamoid bone behind the knee that only some people have.

chapters.text: Name a planet, dwarf planet or moon in our solar system

krillion.quip: A tiny Neptune moon found in old Hubble photos, named for a mythical sea-horse.

quips.Enceladus: Saturn's icy moon sprays water geysers into space from a hidden ocean.
quips.Titan: The only moon with a thick atmosphere and lakes of liquid methane.
quips.Dactyl: The first moon ever found orbiting an asteroid, spotted by Galileo in 1993.

chapters.text: Name one of the 88 official constellations

krillion.quip: The giraffe: Greeks described it as a camel with leopard spots.

quips.Ophiuchus: The serpent bearer: the Sun passes through it, yet it never made the zodiac.
quips.Mensa: The table mountain, named after Table Mountain above Cape Town.
quips.Coma Berenices: Named after a real Egyptian queen's hair, offered to the gods.

chapters.text: Name an organ of the human body

krillion.quip: The fold holding your gut in place was only reclassified as an organ in 2016.

quips.Skin: Your biggest organ, weighing roughly as much as a bowling ball.
quips.Liver: The only internal organ that can regrow from just a quarter of itself.
quips.Appendix: Once called useless, it may store good gut bacteria for emergencies.

krillion.quip: Her pulsing-star rule gave astronomers their first ruler for measuring galaxies.

quips.Rosalind Franklin: Her X-ray Photo 51 revealed DNA's double helix shape.
quips.Mary Anning: A self-taught fossil hunter who found the first full ichthyosaur at about 12.
quips.Hypatia: A mathematician and astronomer who taught in Alexandria around 400 AD.

krillion.quip: An armoured ankylosaur named after the demon dog in Ghostbusters.

quips.Brontosaurus: Sunk as a mistake for a century, it was revived as a real genus in 2015.
quips.Yi: The shortest dinosaur name ever: a small bat-winged climber from China.
quips.Argentinosaurus: Possibly the heaviest land animal ever, at around 70 tonnes.

krillion.quip: MIT students measured a bridge using fellow student Oliver Smoot's body length.

quips.Barn: A tiny area used in nuclear physics; physicists joked a nucleus was as big as a barn.
quips.Shake: Ten nanoseconds, named after a 'shake of a lamb's tail'.
quips.Sverdrup: Measures ocean currents: one sverdrup is a million cubic metres of water per second.

krillion.quip: Its programs are abstract pixel paintings, named after the artist Piet Mondrian.

quips.Malbolge: Designed to be nearly impossible to program; its first 'Hello World' took two years.
quips.Plankalkül: Designed by Konrad Zuse in the 1940s, arguably the first high-level language.
quips.Whitespace: Only spaces, tabs and line breaks count; every other character is ignored.

chapters.text: Name a disease caused by a virus

krillion.quip: Studying this plant blight in the 1890s led scientists to discover viruses.

quips.Smallpox: The only human disease ever fully wiped out, declared eradicated in 1980.
quips.Rinderpest: A cattle plague that became only the second disease ever eradicated, in 2011.
quips.Myxomatosis: Deliberately released in Australia in 1950 to control rabbit numbers.

krillion.quip: Added to the cloud atlas in 2017 after amateur sky-watchers campaigned for it.

quips.Morning Glory: A huge rolling tube cloud that sweeps over northern Australia each spring.
quips.Noctilucent: The highest clouds on Earth, glowing at night about 80 km up.
quips.Virga: Rain that evaporates before it reaches the ground, like wispy streaks.

chapters.text: Name a branch of science ending in -ology

krillion.quip: The scientific study of clouds, from the Greek 'nephos', meaning cloud.

quips.Oology: The study of birds' eggs, once a hugely popular Victorian hobby.
quips.Areology: Geology, but for Mars: named after Ares, the Greek god of war.
quips.Dendrochronology: Dating events by counting and comparing tree rings.

krillion.quip: The fear of peanut butter sticking to the roof of your mouth.

quips.Hippopotomonstrosesquippedaliophobia: The fear of long words, cruelly given one of the longest names possible.
quips.Nomophobia: Fear of being without your phone, short for 'no-mobile-phone phobia'.

chapters.text: Name a famous space mission or spacecraft

krillion.quip: Lost in 1999 because one team used pound-force and the other used newtons.

quips.Voyager 1: The farthest human-made object, now cruising through interstellar space.
quips.Ingenuity: The first aircraft to make a powered, controlled flight on another planet.
quips.Luna 9: The first spacecraft to soft-land on the Moon, in 1966.

krillion.quip: A real London phone maker founded by Carl Pei, so 'Nothing' scores here.

quips.Fairchild Semiconductor: Its founders spun off so many startups they became known as the 'Fairchildren'.
quips.Nokia: Started in 1865 as a paper mill in Finland before it ever made phones.
quips.Nintendo: Founded in 1889 to make hand-made playing cards.

chapters.text: Name an invention of the 20th century

krillion.quip: Percy Shaw got the idea for reflective road studs from a cat's glowing eyes.

quips.Velcro: Inspired by burrs that clung to George de Mestral's dog after a walk in the Alps.
quips.Microwave oven: Discovered when radar engineer Percy Spencer noticed a chocolate bar melting in his pocket.
quips.Bubble wrap: Originally sold as textured wallpaper, which flopped.

chapters.text: Name a muscle in the human body

krillion.quip: Your smallest skeletal muscle, steadying the tiniest bone deep in your ear.

quips.Sartorius: The longest muscle in the body, named after tailors who sat cross-legged.
quips.Palmaris longus: Missing from one or both arms in about one person in seven.
quips.Masseter: Pound for pound, one of the strongest muscles you have: it powers your bite.

krillion.quip: Found in Serbia in 2006 with almost the exact formula of Superman's kryptonite.

quips.Bridgmanite: Earth's most abundant mineral, hidden in the deep mantle and only named in 2014.
quips.Ice: Yes, ice counts: it is naturally occurring, crystalline and inorganic.
quips.Painite: Once the rarest gem on Earth, with fewer than two dozen crystals known in the 2000s.

krillion.quip: A convex 3D shape with one stable resting point; it always rolls itself upright.

quips.Reuleaux triangle: A curved triangle of constant width; it can drill nearly square holes.
quips.Apeirogon: A polygon with infinitely many sides.
quips.Szilassi polyhedron: Seven faces, and every single face touches every other one.

chapters.text: Name a star other than the Sun

krillion.quip: Spotted in 2022 about 12.9 billion years back in time: the most distant single star seen.

quips.Polaris: Not the brightest star, but it sits almost exactly above Earth's North Pole.
quips.Keid: The real star Star Trek picked for Spock's home planet, Vulcan.
quips.Algol: The 'Demon Star' visibly dims every three days as its partner star eclipses it.

chapters.text: Name a piece of science lab equipment

krillion.quip: A three-bulb glass gadget that makes gas on demand and stops when you shut the tap.

quips.Bunsen burner: Popularised by Robert Bunsen in 1855, though his technician did much of the design.
quips.Petri dish: Named after Julius Petri, an assistant to germ pioneer Robert Koch.
quips.Leyden jar: One of the first devices to store electricity, invented in the 1740s.

packs.name: Body & Health
packs.tagline: 21 check-ups · the doctor will see you now

chapters.text: Name a part of the face

krillion.quip: The groove above your upper lip — its name comes from the Greek for 'love charm'.

quips.Glabella: The smooth patch between your eyebrows — doctors tap it to test a reflex.
quips.Cupid's bow: The double curve of your upper lip, named after the archer god's weapon.
quips.Buccinator: The cheek muscle trumpeters rely on — its name comes from the Latin for trumpeter.

chapters.text: Name a type of doctor or medical specialty

krillion.quip: A rehab-medicine doctor — not a psychiatrist, and definitely not a podiatrist.

quips.Veterinarian: Vets train on many species — a GP for humans only has to learn one.
quips.Optometrist: An eye-exam specialist; ophthalmologists are the ones who do eye surgery.
quips.Podiatrist: A foot specialist — the name comes from the Greek for 'foot' and 'healer'.

chapters.text: Name a vitamin or dietary mineral

krillion.quip: You need only a pinch, but it powers enzymes that break down sulfites.

quips.Vitamin C: Humans are among the few mammals that can't make their own vitamin C.
quips.Vitamin D: Your skin makes it from sunlight, which is why it's nicknamed the sunshine vitamin.
quips.Cobalt: It sits at the heart of the vitamin B12 molecule — the only vitamin with a metal core.

chapters.text: Name a gym or bodyweight exercise

krillion.quip: Bruce Lee's signature core move — your whole body levers up off a bench like a flag.

quips.Burpee: Named after physiologist Royal Burpee, who invented it in the 1930s as a fitness test.
quips.Jumping jack: Legend credits US Army general John 'Black Jack' Pershing with popularising it.
quips.Planche: A gymnast's hold where your whole body hovers flat, balanced only on your hands.

chapters.text: Name something you'd find in a first-aid kit

krillion.quip: A tiny hooked tool that twists ticks out cleanly — a staple of hikers' kits.

quips.Plaster: The Band-Aid was invented in 1920 by a Johnson & Johnson employee for his accident-prone wife.
quips.Triangular bandage: One cloth, a dozen uses: sling, pad, tie or even a makeshift tourniquet.

chapters.text: Name a part of the human eye

krillion.quip: The pink fold in your eye's inner corner — a leftover of a third eyelid.

quips.Cornea: It has no blood vessels at all — it takes its oxygen straight from the air.
quips.Optic disc: No photoreceptors sit here, so your brain quietly paints over the blind spot.
quips.Dua's layer: A thin layer of the cornea first described only in 2013.

chapters.text: Name a sleep disorder or something that can happen in your sleep

krillion.quip: Sleep groaning: long, eerie moans on each out-breath that the sleeper never hears.

quips.Narcolepsy: Some people with it collapse when they laugh, as strong emotions switch their muscles off.
quips.Exploding head syndrome: A harmless but startling 'bang' heard as you drift off — no headache involved.
quips.Hypnic jerk: That falling-feeling twitch as you drop off — most people get one now and then.

chapters.text: Name a hormone in the human body

krillion.quip: Named after Hershey's Kisses — it was discovered in Hershey, Pennsylvania.

quips.Oxytocin: Nicknamed the 'cuddle hormone' — it's released during hugs and childbirth.
quips.Ghrelin: Your 'hunger hormone': levels climb before meals and fall once you've eaten.
quips.Melatonin: Your body releases it as darkness falls, nudging you toward sleep.
quips.Irisin: Released by exercising muscle, it's named after Iris, the Greek messenger goddess.

chapters.text: Name a part of the brain

krillion.quip: Latin for 'tree of life' — the branching white matter inside your cerebellum.

deepcut: Bed nucleus of the stria terminalis

quips.Hippocampus: Named after the seahorse, which early anatomists thought it resembled.
quips.Amygdala: From the Greek for 'almond' — it's an almond-shaped hub for fear and emotion.
quips.Claustrum: A thin sheet of neurons that Francis Crick suspected might help bind consciousness.
quips.Pineal gland: Descartes called it the seat of the soul; it actually makes melatonin.

chapters.text: Name a joint in the human body (or a type of joint)

krillion.quip: The peg-in-socket joint that anchors each of your teeth in the jaw.

quips.Saddle joint: Your thumb's base sits in a saddle joint — the secret behind gripping with opposable thumbs.
quips.Pubic symphysis: It loosens during pregnancy, helped along by the hormone relaxin.
quips.Suture: Skull bones meet at wiggly suture joints that fuse slowly as you age.

chapters.text: Name a piece of medical equipment or a medical instrument

krillion.quip: A trumpet-shaped tube midwives press to the bump to hear a baby's heartbeat.

quips.Stethoscope: Invented in 1816 by René Laennec, whose first version was a rolled-up tube of paper.
quips.Iron lung: A whole-body breathing chamber that saved thousands during the polio epidemics.
quips.Defibrillator: It doesn't restart a stopped heart — it resets one that's quivering out of rhythm.

krillion.quip: A sudden calf-muscle tear named after the sport where lunging so often causes it.

quips.Tennis elbow: Most people who get tennis elbow have never picked up a racket.
quips.Cauliflower ear: Blood pools under the ear's skin after repeated blows and hardens into bumps.
quips.Turf toe: A big-toe sprain that became common once American football moved onto artificial turf.

chapters.text: Name a part of the ear

krillion.quip: A small bump on some people's ear rim that Darwin wrote about as an evolutionary leftover.

quips.Stapes: The smallest bone in your body — about the size of a grain of rice.
quips.Otoliths: Tiny calcium crystals in your inner ear that tell your brain which way is down.
quips.Tragus: The little flap in front of your ear canal — press it to muffle sound.

chapters.text: Name a nerve in the human body

krillion.quip: A tiny vagus branch nicknamed 'criminal' for letting ulcers return after surgery.

deepcut: Medial cutaneous nerve of the forearm
Lateral cutaneous nerve of the forearm
Medial cutaneous nerve of the arm
Dorsal cutaneous branch of the ulnar nerve

Lateral femoral cutaneous nerve: Lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh
Posterior femoral cutaneous nerve: Posterior cutaneous nerve of the thigh
Arnold's nerve: Auricular branch of the vagus nerve
Superficial radial nerve: Superficial branch of the radial nerve

quips.Ulnar nerve: Hitting your 'funny bone' is really whacking this exposed nerve at the elbow.
quips.Vagus nerve: Its name means 'wandering' — it meanders from your brainstem all the way to your gut.
quips.Sciatic nerve: The longest and widest nerve in your body — about as thick as your thumb at its widest.
quips.Terminal nerve: Sometimes called 'cranial nerve zero', it was discovered after the other twelve were numbered.

chapters.text: Name a gland in the human body

krillion.quip: Tiny glands at the back of your tongue that rinse your taste buds clean between bites.

quips.Liver: The body's largest gland as well as its largest internal organ.
quips.Pineal gland: It's shaped like a tiny pine cone, which is how it got its name.
quips.Thymus: It trains your T cells, then slowly shrinks and turns to fat after puberty.

chapters.text: Name a type of cell in the human body

krillion.quip: Brain cells that fire when you're in one particular spot — your built-in GPS.

quips.Red blood cell: They ditch their nucleus as they mature, leaving more room for oxygen-carrying haemoglobin.
quips.Egg cell: The largest cell in the human body — just about visible to the naked eye.
quips.Osteoclast: A bone-dissolving cell that constantly remodels your skeleton.
quips.Grid cell: Neurons that fire in a hexagonal grid pattern as you move around — Nobel-winning stuff.

chapters.text: Name a reflex or involuntary body action

krillion.quip: Poking inside your ear makes some people cough, thanks to a branch of the vagus nerve.

quips.Yawn: Yawning is contagious — even reading about it can set you off.
quips.Photic sneeze reflex: Bright light makes roughly one in four people sneeze — it's nicknamed ACHOO syndrome.
quips.Diving reflex: Cold water on your face slows your heart — a built-in trick for holding your breath.

chapters.text: Name a part of the hand or foot

krillion.quip: The hollow at the base of your thumb, named for where people once rested a pinch of snuff.

deepcut: Ulnar collateral ligament of the thumb

quips.Lunula: The pale half-moon at the base of your nail — its name is Latin for 'little moon'.
quips.Fingerprint: Even identical twins have different fingerprints.
quips.Pisiform: The pea-shaped wrist bone sits inside a tendon, just as your kneecap does.

chapters.text: Name a medical test or scan

krillion.quip: A paper strip hooked under your lower eyelid measures how many tears you make.

quips.X-ray: Wilhelm Röntgen's first X-ray photo showed his wife's hand — wedding ring and all.
quips.Heel prick test: A few drops from a newborn's heel can screen for several rare but treatable conditions.
quips.Pap smear: Named after Georgios Papanikolaou, the Greek doctor who developed it.

chapters.text: Name a medicine (generic or brand name)

krillion.quip: A heart drug made from foxglove, a plant whose heart effects were described back in 1785.

quips.Penicillin: Alexander Fleming spotted it in 1928 when mould spoiled one of his bacteria dishes.
quips.Aspirin: Its ancestor, salicin, comes from willow bark — used for pain since ancient times.
quips.Quinine: Extracted from cinchona bark, it's what gives tonic water its bitter bite.

chapters.text: Name an artery or vein in the human body

krillion.quip: A deep brain vein named after Galen, the Roman-era Greek doctor who dissected apes.

quips.Aorta: Your body's biggest artery — at its start it's about as wide as a garden hose.
quips.Great saphenous vein: The longest vein in your body, running from the top of your foot to your groin.
quips.Pulmonary artery: Unlike most arteries, they carry oxygen-poor blood — from the heart to the lungs.

packs.name: History & Myth
packs.tagline: 21 relics · dust off the old stories

krillion.quip: The first president born a US citizen — and he grew up speaking Dutch.

quips.William Henry Harrison: He served just 31 days — the shortest presidency ever.
quips.Grover Cleveland: For over a century the only president with two non-consecutive terms.

chapters.text: Name a Greek god or goddess

krillion.quip: Primordial goddess of night — Homer says even Zeus feared to anger her.

quips.Hecate: Goddess of crossroads and witchcraft, often shown with three faces.
quips.Nike: Goddess of victory — the sportswear brand borrowed her name.
quips.Momus: God of mockery, so critical the gods threw him out of Olympus.

krillion.quip: Painted abstract art before Kandinsky, but asked that it stay hidden for decades.

quips.Bob Ross: Painted over 30,000 canvases and never once lost his calm.
quips.Raphael: Died at 37, yet ranks with Leonardo and Michelangelo in the Renaissance trinity.

krillion.quip: Co-written with John Fletcher and based on Chaucer's The Knight's Tale.

Edward III: The Reign of King Edward the Third

quips.Edward III: Only accepted into the Shakespeare canon in the 1990s.
quips.Titus Andronicus: His bloodiest play — two villains end up baked into a pie.

krillion.quip: He bought the throne at auction from the Praetorian Guard in AD 193.

quips.Caligula: Ancient gossip claims he planned to make his horse Incitatus a consul.
quips.Romulus Augustulus: The last Western emperor, deposed as a teenager in AD 476.
quips.Constantine XI Palaiologos: The last Byzantine emperor, killed defending Constantinople in 1453.

krillion.quip: A Bavarian horned, winged rabbit — taxidermists still stitch together 'specimens'.

quips.Bunyip: An Australian swamp monster said to lurk in billabongs and waterholes.
quips.Tarasque: A Provençal dragon-turtle, tamed in legend by Saint Martha.
quips.Kappa: Japanese water imp — bow to it, and it bows back, spilling its powers.

krillion.quip: A Greek from Marseille who sailed to Britain c. 325 BC and wrote of distant 'Thule'.

rare: René-Robert Cavelier, Sieur de La Salle

quips.Leif Erikson: Reached North America around 1000 AD, nearly 500 years before Columbus.
quips.Matthew Henson: Peary's African American partner on the famous 1909 North Pole expedition.

chapters.text: Name an English or British monarch

krillion.quip: King of England who collapsed and died mid-toast at a wedding feast in 1042.

quips.Lady Jane Grey: Queen for just nine days in 1553 before Mary I took the throne.
quips.Edward VIII: Abdicated after less than a year to marry Wallis Simpson.
quips.Athelstan: Usually counted as the first King of all England, from 927.

chapters.text: Name a Norse god or goddess

krillion.quip: Odin's son who rode Sleipnir down to Hel to beg for Baldur's return.

quips.Hel: Loki's daughter, ruler of the dead — half her body was said to be blue-black.
quips.Bragi: God of poetry, said to have runes carved on his tongue.
quips.Kvasir: So wise that, after his murder, his blood was brewed into the mead of poetry.

krillion.quip: Saharan farmers who tapped hidden groundwater with long tunnels called foggaras.

quips.Norte Chico: Built pyramids in Peru around the same era as Egypt's first pyramids.
quips.Minoans: Bronze Age Cretans famous for bull-leaping frescoes at Knossos.

krillion.quip: In 751 the Abbasids beat Tang China; legend says captive papermakers took paper west.

rare: Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa
Battle of the Plains of Abraham

quips.Battle of Thermopylae: 300 Spartans and several thousand other Greeks held the pass for three days.
quips.Battle of Hastings: 1066 — Harold II was killed, traditionally by an arrow to the eye.
quips.Battle of Rorke's Drift: About 150 defenders held off thousands; eleven Victoria Crosses followed.

krillion.quip: A Cynic who married Crates and lived on the streets of Athens as his equal.

quips.Diogenes: Lived in a large jar and told Alexander the Great to stop blocking his sun.
quips.Thales: Often called the first philosopher; he reportedly predicted a solar eclipse.

chapters.text: Name an ancient Egyptian god or goddess

krillion.quip: An obscure 'smiter' from the Book of the Dead, drawn like a sheet-ghost with eyes.

quips.Bes: A dwarf god who protected households, mothers and children from evil.
quips.Taweret: Part hippo, part crocodile, part lion — and the guardian of childbirth.
quips.Apep: Giant serpent of chaos who attacked Ra's sun boat every night.

chapters.text: Name a hero of Greek mythology

krillion.quip: Amazon queen at Troy — Achilles killed her, then fell for her as she died.

quips.Bellerophon: Tamed Pegasus to slay the Chimera, then flew too high and was thrown.
quips.Atalanta: A huntress who lost a footrace only because she stopped for golden apples.

chapters.text: Name a knight of the Round Table

krillion.quip: King Arthur's court jester, knighted as a joke — yet he took a seat at the Table.

Ironside: Red Knight of the Red Lands

quips.Galahad: The purest knight, and the one who finally achieved the Holy Grail.
quips.Mordred: Arthur's nephew (or son) whose rebellion ended Camelot at Camlann.

chapters.text: Name a Nobel Peace Prize laureate

krillion.quip: An agronomist whose high-yield wheat is credited with saving up to a billion lives.

schooler: International Committee of the Red Cross
rare: Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons
deepcut: International Physicians for the Prevention of Nuclear War

ICAN: International Campaign to Abolish Nuclear Weapons

quips.Linus Pauling: The only person to win two unshared Nobels — Chemistry and Peace.
quips.Henry Dunant: Founder of the Red Cross and joint winner of the very first Peace Prize in 1901.

krillion.quip: King from the moment of his birth in 1316 — he lived just five days.

quips.Louis XIV: Reigned 72 years, the longest of any monarch of a major European country.
quips.Louis XVIII: Named XVIII because royalists counted Louis XVI's son as Louis XVII.

chapters.text: Name a famous real ship from history

krillion.quip: Sank in 1628 less than a mile into its maiden voyage — then was raised intact in 1961.

quips.Mary Celeste: Found adrift in 1872 in good order, with not a soul aboard.
quips.Cutty Sark: One of the fastest tea clippers ever, now dry-docked in Greenwich.

krillion.quip: A Byzantine splinter state that outlived Constantinople's fall by eight years.

quips.Holy Roman Empire: Voltaire quipped it was neither holy, nor Roman, nor an empire.
quips.Mongol Empire: The largest contiguous land empire in history.

chapters.text: Name a real pirate from history

krillion.quip: A Breton noblewoman who raided French ships for 13 years to avenge her husband.

quips.Ching Shih: Commanded a pirate fleet of tens of thousands, then negotiated a peaceful retirement.
quips.Stede Bonnet: A wealthy landowner who bought a ship and turned pirate with no sailing experience.

krillion.quip: The first securely attested female pharaoh, ruling centuries before Hatshepsut.

quips.Hatshepsut: Ruled as king for about two decades and was often depicted with a false beard.
quips.Khufu: Built the Great Pyramid, yet the only certain statue of him is 7.5 cm tall.

quips.Cinderella: In the Grimm version, the stepsisters cut off bits of their feet to fit the shoe.

Charlie and the Great Glass Elevator

The Wonderful Story of Henry Sugar

quips.Augustus Gloop: First child out of the tour — sucked up a pipe after falling in the chocolate river.
quips.Fleshlumpeater: The biggest, nastiest of the BFG's nine giant brothers.

chapters.text: Name a spell from Harry Potter

krillion.quip: Lockhart's pixie-catching spell in Chamber of Secrets — it did absolutely nothing.

chapters.text: Name a character from Alice in Wonderland or Through the Looking-Glass

krillion.quip: A Looking-Glass insect with a crust body and a sugar-lump head that lives on weak tea.

quips.Cheshire Cat: It fades away until only its grin is left hanging in the air.
quips.Dodo: Often read as Carroll's self-portrait — his real name, Dodgson, came out as 'Do-Do-Dodgson'.
quips.Duck: A nod to Robinson Duckworth, who rowed with Carroll the day the story was first told.

krillion.quip: Wilkie Collins' rose-loving sleuth in The Moonstone, one of fiction's first detectives.

quips.Hercule Poirot: The only fictional character ever given a front-page obituary in The New York Times.
quips.C. Auguste Dupin: Poe's Paris sleuth from 1841 — the template Sherlock Holmes was built on.

chapters.text: Name a character from The Hunger Games

krillion.quip: Prim's beloved goat — her milk and cheese helped keep the Everdeens fed.

quips.Rue: Katniss covered her body in flowers — a quiet act of defiance that sparked an uprising.
quips.Cinna: The stylist who turned Katniss into 'the girl who was on fire.'
